records.reason: Low-width m24 control at 2/1. It anchors routine hydrocarbon behavior and helps keep late-tail corrections from spreading into ordinary weakly polar rows.
High-width m0 point at 10/1. The brominated triphenyl alkene probes whether a nonpolar fused or highly aromatic graph can enter a distinct high-ratio endpoint regime.

m39 at 20/1 has broad model ranges and a carbonyl-rich oxygenated aromatic graph. It targets endpoint shape under strong eluent while sampling a different graph from the multifunctional ester failures.
m128 sulfur-containing aryl ketone at 5/1. This intermediate-ratio point can locate the onset of sulfur-associated late behavior before extrapolating to more extreme conditions.
Low-width m118 aldehyde control at 0/1. It provides an ordinary oxygenated aromatic boundary for calibrating early endpoints.
m80 at 10/1 with low sample volume is a compact ester control. It tests whether high-ratio ester behavior remains routine when loading is reduced.
m37 at 1/1 is a nitro ketone point with broad model ranges. It probes carbonyl endpoint broadening at moderate eluent strength before high-ratio extrapolation.
m89 aniline ester at 5/1 samples donor-containing ester chemistry at an intermediate ratio. It tests whether donor effects produce a broad V2 response outside the most extreme multifunctional rows.
m84 at 30/1 is a high-ratio halogenated ester point with substantial model width. It separates general ratio effects from donor-rich and multifunctional ester behavior.
Low-width m63 fused ketone at 0/1. It calibrates a compact fused carbonyl boundary against high-ratio fused and diaryl candidates.
m21 at 1/1 is a routine ether-containing acrylate. It adds bulk-distribution coverage for compact oxygenated chemistry.
m101 at 5/1 samples a bromomethyl aromatic ester at a moderate ratio. It tests transfer across halogenated ester structures without selecting only extreme model widths.
m184 at 20/1 is a high-ratio dibromo aldehyde with wide endpoint uncertainty. It probes whether heavy halogenation and aromatic carbonyl structure create a late-tail regime.
Low-width m133 alkylbenzene at 5/1. It is a neutral interpolation control near the high-ratio aromatic experiments.
m202 at 1/1 is a low-ratio phosphorus-containing anchor. It tests whether the unusual phosphorus response is activated only by stronger eluent or higher loading.
m9 at 0/1 is a low-width neutral biphenyl control. It helps calibrate early retention for nonpolar aromatic systems.
m28 at 1/1 has broad endpoint ranges and a multifunctional aromatic aldehyde/ester graph. It supplies an intermediate condition point for carbonyl-rich endpoint-shape learning.
m49 at 20/1 probes a hindered aromatic aldehyde under strong eluent. It tests whether high-ratio broadening extends to less polar carbonyl graphs.
m23 at 2/1 is a moderate-ratio neutral ester control. Paired with the selected 50/1 m23 point, it forms a meaningful same-molecule ratio-response experiment.
m64 at 5/1 is a halogenated aryl ketone at intermediate strength. It helps calibrate the boundary between ordinary ketone behavior and broad carbonyl tails.
m23 at 50/1 extends the same-molecule m23 curve into extreme solvent ratio. The paired labels can test whether neutral ester responses remain smooth at high ratio.
Low-width m110 trimethoxy aromatic ether at 0/1. It provides a compact oxygenated control distinct from donor-containing carbonyls.
m80 at 10/1 with higher sample volume complements the low-volume m80 point. The pair directly tests loading effects in a compact ester regime.
m88 amino ester at 0/1 probes donor-containing ester behavior at weak eluent. It provides a lower-ratio anchor for separating hydrogen-bonding effects from high-ratio endpoint broadening.
m140 halogenated neutral aromatic at 10/1 is a compact high-ratio control. It tests polarity-independent ratio scaling and protects against overcorrection for heavy aromatic structures.
m174 diaryl ester at 10/1 provides an ordinary high-ratio aromatic carbonyl point. It helps distinguish broad multifunctional tails from general diaryl retention.
m10 neutral diaryl alkene at 50/1 samples an extreme ratio with no heteroatom donors or acceptors. It is a useful polarity-independent control for solvent-strength scaling.
m124 fused oxygenated aromatic at 0/1 is a low-width early boundary. It tests whether fused-ring corrections should apply at weak eluent in otherwise compact chemistry.
m83 aromatic ester at 5/1 adds routine ester coverage at moderate ratio and loading. It helps preserve interpolation accuracy across the common catalog chemistry.
m126 anisole-like control at 0/1 has a narrow predicted interval. It anchors ordinary weak-eluent behavior for simple aromatic ethers.
m128 sulfur ketone at 2/1 supplies a lower-ratio companion to the selected 5/1 m128 point. The pair can distinguish smooth sulfur-ketone response from a ratio-triggered transition.
m209 donor-containing aryl ether at 1/1 tests hydrogen-bonding and loading effects in a compact-side regime. It broadens donor chemistry without relying only on extreme predicted tails.

hypotheses.content: Carbonyl-rich, donor-containing, and multifunctional aromatic molecules require condition-dependent endpoint-shape corrections; V2 can broaden or shift independently of V1.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The batch samples carbonyl, donor, ester, phosphorus, and nitro motifs across condition strengths and loading levels, allowing retraining to learn endpoint-specific interactions without applying a global late correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do loading and solvent ratio explain endpoint broadening across these families, or are graph-specific interactions required?

hypotheses.content: High-ratio conditions create molecule-family-specific regimes in fused, diaryl, sulfur-containing, and heteroaromatic systems, while neutral controls can remain compact.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The batch includes high-ratio neutral, fused, sulfur, halogenated, and diaryl candidates plus lower-ratio companions, which can teach when solvent-strength scaling transfers across graph classes.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are late high-ratio endpoints driven mainly by ring fusion and heteroatoms, or by a broader condition response shared with neutral diaryl systems?

hypotheses.content: Low-width ordinary controls are needed to calibrate the boundary between routine interpolation and difficult late-tail regions.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Controls in this batch cover simple hydrocarbons, ethers, esters, ketones, and halogenated neutrals so that retraining can repair difficult regimes while preserving accuracy in the routine portion of the Row-distribution.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which structural and condition features mark the boundary between compact routine behavior and broad late tails?

feedback_interpretation: Recent measurements reinforced that V2 endpoint shape and condition response drive the largest failures. Severe tails occurred in multifunctional esters, donor-rich molecules, fused systems, phosphorus-containing chemistry, and azaaromatic or nitrile-containing structures, while several neutral controls remained compact. The new batch therefore combines high-ratio regime tests with same-molecule m23 and m80 response pairs and a broad set of compact controls.
batch_rationale: The 32 candidates combine endpoint-tail repair, high-ratio regime exploration, loading-response comparisons, and routine calibration. The m23 and m80 pairs provide local condition or loading experiments; m128, m184, m49, m202, and m10 probe high-ratio structure-condition interactions; m37, m89, m88, m28, m174, and m209 cover donor and carbonyl endpoint shape; and simple hydrocarbon, ether, ester, ketone, and neutral aromatic controls protect the bulk Row-distribution from overgeneralized corrections. All selected IDs are distinct candidate rows from the supplied pool.
